extracted.intended_audience: scholars, teachers, writers, and educational or research organizations seeking NEH research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program-level criteria for projects seeking funding from the NEH Division of Research, describing the kinds of humanities research, formats, audiences, and institutional configurations the Division supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for advanced humanities research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division of Research supports advanced humanities research by making grants to scholars, teachers and writers, and to educational and research organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should engage in substantive humanities research activities — examples given include editions of the Dead Sea Scrolls, a book on the history of 'The Star Spangled Banner,' and the autobiography of Mark Twain — and may be carried out by individuals or collaborative teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project activities and approaches the Division funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division supports projects that explore archives, interpret humanities texts and materials, develop and use digital tools, discover new knowledge or rediscover truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should frame projects around one or more of these activities (archival exploration, textual interpretation, digital tool development/use, original discovery or reinterpretation) to align with the Division's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioning studies on the state of the humanities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Division also supports the humanities by commissioning studies on the state of the humanities to assess Americans’ engagement with the humanities and monitor trends within individual fields of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that aim to evaluate public engagement, field trends, or that propose rigorous studies of the state of particular humanities disciplines align with this programmatic function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Scholars (audience and format expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Scholars: Supports well-researched books in the humanities intended to reach a broad readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aimed at producing book-length work that is both scholarly and accessible to general readers — i.e., with clear public-facing dissemination goals — are appropriate for this program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships (individual advanced research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships: Supports individuals pursuing advanced research that is of value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship proposals should demonstrate individual scholarly merit and explain the anticipated value to academic audiences, general audiences, or a combination of both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly Editions and Translations (textual preservation/access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly Editions and Translations: Supports the preparation of editions and translations of pre-existing texts of value to the humanities that are currently inaccessible or available only in inadequate editions or transcriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should justify the text’s value to the field and demonstrate that the edition/translation will address inaccessibility or inadequacy in existing versions; technical editorial/transcription plans and standards of scholarly apparatus are implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative Research (team-based, sustained projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborative Research: Supports groups of two or more scholars engaging in significant and sustained research in the humanities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be team-based, demonstrate sustained collaboration (rather than short-term partnerships), and outline how multiple scholars will contribute to a coherent research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards for Faculty at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards for Faculty at Historically Black Colleges and Universities: Supports individual faculty or staff members at HBCUs pursuing research of value to humanities scholars, students, or general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and project framing should reflect affiliation with an HBCU and emphasize the research’s value to scholars, students, or broader audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships for Advanced Social Science Research on Japan (topical scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships for Advanced Social Science Research on Japan: Supports research on modern Japanese society and political economy, Japan's international relations, and U.S.-Japan relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should focus on the specified topical areas (modern Japanese society, political economy, international relations, or U.S.-Japan relations) to fit this program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of public and educational impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Research projects add to the existing store of knowledge and reach all Americans; teachers and media makers rely on new research findings in many fields to educate, inform, and inspire their audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should articulate how their project will contribute to public understanding, educational use, or broader dissemination (e.g., outputs useful to teachers, media makers, or general audiences).
